# Review of e43656228da5: `omp gc --archive` keeps an archived session resumable and its rows intact

I ran three probes against the real production functions: `runGcCommand`, `SessionManager.open`, `resolveResumableSession` and `FileSessionStorage.deleteSessionWithArtifacts`. Each found a defect. ## P0 — Stop `omp gc --reclaim` from deleting a session that an open but not-yet-written `SessionManager` holds, which leaves a transcript with no header

**Where:** `packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gc-cli.ts:2411-2455` (`runReclaimGc`: leases, then the proof, then `removeProvenLiveTree` and `fs.unlink(sessionPath)`). It depends on `src/session/session-manager.ts:1111-1128` (`#claimSession`: "Only write paths claim").

**Mechanism:** The changelog says reclaim "takes the ownership leases of the whole session tree … before it proves the archive holds the live copy", so an owner cannot write between the proof and the deletion. That assumes every process with the session open holds a lease. It does not. `SessionManager` claims the lease only on its first write. A user who has resumed a cold session and not typed yet holds no lease.

So `runReclaimGc` gets the leases, proves the tree and unlinks the transcript and the artifact tree. When the user then types, `#claimSession` succeeds because reclaim has released its leases. The writer appends to the deleted path and creates a new `.jsonl` that contains only the new entry: no session header and no earlier history.

That file is the live transcript now:
- The archive is not a prefix of it.
- Reopening goes through `materializeSessionFile` → `restoreArchivedSessionLocked`, which refuses.
- The session's tool output and subagent transcripts are gone from the live tree.

**Trigger** (`reclaim-open.test.ts`):
1. Write an idle session with `<artifacts>/out.txt` and run `gc --archive --apply`.
2. `SessionManager.open(file)`.
3. `runGcCommand({ reclaim: ID, apply: true, forwardOnly: true })`.
4. `sm.appendMessage(...)`, then `sm.flush()`.
5. `SessionManager.open(file)` again.

**Measured:**
```
A opened: true entries: 2
reclaimed: 1 errors: []
live after reclaim: false artifact: false
live after A writes: true
live content:
{"type":"message","id":"6d8bfc80","parentId":"m2","timestamp":"2026-10-30T13:11:23.223Z","runtime":{"version":"18.14.0"},"message":{"role":"user","content":"next turn","timestamp":1793365883223}}

artifact after A writes: false
archive exists: true
reopen: ERROR Cannot restore ".../archive/sessions/--work--/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01a18630-....jsonl.gz": a running process owns this session or one of its subagent sessions. Close it and run `omp gc --restore 01a18630-42ae-7117-ba7c-029b1eee0f4b --apply --agent-dir ...` again.
```

The reopen error is from the same process still holding its lease. I did not measure what a restore does after A exits. Reading the code, `restoreArchivedSessionLocked` (session-archive.ts:1122) would then refuse "over a different session file", because the archive is not a prefix of a file that has no header. In both cases the new turn sits in a corrupt transcript that nothing will merge back.

## P1 — Make session deletion also remove the archived copy that `gc --archive` now keeps

**Where:** `packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-storage.ts:1370-1407` (`deleteSessionWithArtifacts`, used by the picker, `/delete` and `main.ts:238`). It becomes reachable through `src/session/session-listing.ts:1480-1501` (the new archive fallback in `resolveResumableSession`) and `src/session/session-archive.ts:1257` (`materializeSessionFile`).

**Mechanism:** Before this patch, `gc --archive` moved the session out, so nobody could delete it from the picker. Now it copies the session and keeps the live one, so the session is still listed and deletable. Deletion removes only the live `.jsonl`, its artifact directory and `.bak` files. The gzip and archived artifact tree under `archive/sessions/` stay.

The next `omp --resume <id>` finds no live match and falls back to `findArchivedSessionFiles`. `SessionManager.open` then restores the deleted transcript and artifacts into the sessions tree. A session the user deleted, contents included, comes back without a word.

**Trigger** (`resurrect.test.ts`):
1. Write a cold session whose prompt contains `SECRET-TOKEN-abc`, plus an artifact.
2. Run `gc --archive --apply`.
3. `new FileSessionStorage().deleteSessionWithArtifacts(file)`.
4. `resolveResumableSession(ID, root)`, then `SessionManager.open(match.session.path)`.

**Measured:**
```
archived: 1 errors: []
live exists after delete: false
resolve after delete: archive /…/probe-resurrect-gNcpGf/archive/sessions/--work--/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01a18630-42ae-7117-ba7c-029b1eee0f4b.jsonl.gz
reopened at: /…/probe-resurrect-gNcpGf/sessions/--work--/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01a18630-42ae-7117-ba7c-029b1eee0f4b.jsonl
live exists after resume: true
content contains secret: true
artifact back: true
```

## P2 — Stop an ordinary open from bringing back artifacts the live session deleted after it was archived

**Where:** `packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-archive.ts:1217-1234` (`liveSessionIsComplete`) and `:1266-1274`. Every open reaches it through the new unconditional `materializeSessionFile` call in `session-manager.ts` `setSessionFile`.

**Mechanism:** The changelog says an open "does not mistake a session that carried on since it was archived … for an interrupted restore". That is not true when the live session deletes a file. `liveSessionIsComplete` returns `false` for any archived file with no live counterpart. The open then takes the gc lock and the session leases and calls `copyTreeDereferenced`, which copies the deleted file back.

A real case: `removeAnnotationDraft` (`extensibility/custom-commands/bundled/annotate/draft-store.ts:96-101`) deletes `<artifacts>/annotation-drafts/<id>/draft-*.json`. Every later open of the session, until it is archived again, brings back the draft the user already submitted or discarded. Because each such open also goes through `restoreArchivedSession`, it:
- waits up to 30 s behind any `omp gc` run;
- fails if another process holds a lease on any nested subagent session.

**Trigger** (`revive.test.ts`): archive a session with `<artifacts>/annotate/draft-x.json`, `fs.rm` the draft, then `SessionManager.open(file)`. The probe used a slightly different path from the real draft directory; the code path is the same for any artifact file.

**Measured:**
```
archived: 1 []
draft exists before open: false
opened: /…/sessions/--work--/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_01a18630-42ae-7117-ba7c-029b1eee0f4b.jsonl
draft exists after open: true
```

---

**Verdict: not safe to merge.** The only deleting step, `--reclaim`, can leave a live transcript with no header, measured in the P0 probe. Separately, the copy that `gc --archive` now keeps brings back sessions and artifacts that users deleted.
